Subject: Redwood next steps / procurement info

Hi Marissa -

Thanks again for the demo today. Acme is interested in moving forward pending procurement and legal review. A few quick questions to help our team kick off vendor setup:

- Can you send a vendor setup packet (W-9, sample invoice, primary contact, banking instructions)?
- Do you support Purchase Orders (POs) or do you require credit card payments for initial billing?
- Is Redwood available on any cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace)? Our procurement prefers marketplace purchases when available.

If you can send the packet and confirm who our finance contact should work with, we can start the vendor intake. Ideally we'd have the vendor packet back by the end of next week (Aug 20).

Best,
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Integrations
Acme Analytics

Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700

Jordan - great to hear. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Vendor packet: attaching our standard vendor_setup_packet.pdf, Redwood W-9 (W-9_Redwood.pdf), and a sample invoice (sample_invoice.pdf).
- Payment: we support both POs and card. For enterprise deals we typically accept PO + net terms (Net 30/45) for signed contracts; card is fine for self-serve or early pilots. Please let me know which your team prefers.
- Marketplaces: Redwood is in the process of listing on AWS Marketplace; we have a public listing coming Q3, but not fully GA yet. We can discuss marketplace billing if you need that flow.

If Acme prefers PO + Net 45, we'll coordinate contracting and finance can accept PO numbers on invoices. If you'd like, I can loop in our finance lead (Sean Gallagher) to confirm banking instructions and KYC details for your vendor portal.

Next steps:
1) Confirm PO vs card and preferred payment terms.
2) If PO, send vendor portal link or vendor intake form and I'll have Sean fill in bank details.
3) I'll route the MSA to you via DocuSign if legal prefers.

I’ve attached the packet here. Let me know if the procurement team needs anything else.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the packet. A couple items from our side:

- Acme requires a completed vendor intake form (attached: acme_vendor_form.pdf) plus a current W-9 (you included that, thank you).
- For payment we prefer Purchase Orders with Net 45 terms for new vendors. Please confirm you can accept PO numbers on invoices and Net 45.
- We require banking details for ACH setup. We cannot accept bank account numbers over email; please advise if you have a secure vendor portal where we can submit ACH details or whether you can provide a secure upload link.
- Marketplace: we prefer marketplace procurement, but if Redwood is not GA on AWS Marketplace yet, we will proceed via PO. If/when you are GA, we may migrate future purchases there.

Can you provide a primary finance contact to coordinate vendor portal access and ACH onboarding? If you can send the MSA (for our legal review) via DocuSign that would speed things up.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Redwood next steps / procurement info

Thanks - looping in our finance and marketplace leads to move this forward. See actions below and inline answers to your asks.

- PO + Net 45: Confirmed. Redwood accepts PO numbers on invoices and can agree to Net 45 for this account. Sean (cc) will confirm final billing contact details and provide the secure upload method for banking/ACH.
- Vendor intake form: I received acme_vendor_form.pdf and will have Sean fill it out this week.
- ACH/banking: Sean, can you share the secure upload link we should use for Acme (or confirm if you prefer we send a secure DocuSign envelope)?
- MSA/DocuSign: I will route the MSA to Jordan and Acme legal via DocuSign once Sean confirms finance fields.
- Marketplace: Camila, can you confirm expected GA timing for AWS Marketplace and whether we can provide any interim marketplace identifiers for procurement?

Timeline: Sean to complete vendor form + banking upload by Fri Aug 21. I’ll follow up with Acme on Aug 22 to confirm receipt and next steps for signatures/invoice.

Marissa Cole
